title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
subtitle: British steamed sponge with grated apple and warm toffee sauce
excerpt: A moist sponge made with grated apple and honey, served drenched in a warm butter and cream toffee sauce. A British classic that is much simpler to make than it looks.
sourceNotes: Sticky toffee pudding is a modern British classic, popularised in the 1970s at the Sharrow Bay Hotel in the Lake District. Traditional recipes use dates for moisture; grated apple provides a similar effect here.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the sponge up to a day ahead. Make the sauce fresh and pour over to reheat.

content.text: Grate the apple coarsely and leave it in the batter without squeezing; the moisture is what makes the sponge tender.

items.prepNote: 80g softened for sponge; 40g for toffee sauce
about 2 medium apples, peeled and coarsely grated

content.text: Heat the oven to 180°C. Butter a 20x20cm baking dish or 4 individual pudding moulds.
Beat 80g softened butter with the honey until pale.
Beat in the eggs one at a time.
Fold in the flour, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt.
Stir in the milk and grated apple until just combined.
Pour into the prepared dish and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
For the sauce, melt 40g butter in a small saucepan over a medium heat.
Add the double cream and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened.
Pour the sauce over the sponge and serve immediately.

items.cause: Overmixing after adding the flour develops gluten.
items.fix: Fold, do not beat, once the flour goes in.

items.symptom: Sponge is too moist in the centre.
items.cause: Underbaked or apple had too much moisture.
items.fix: Return to oven for 5 more minutes; test with a clean skewer.
Remove from heat immediately, stir in a splash of cold cream.
